bodySections.heading: Why timing matters for this schedule
paragraphs: Colostrum fade is the clock behind this Spanish Water Dog table, and doses at 8, 12, 16, 16 weeks exist to immunize the puppy while exposure (parks, foster homes, boarding intros) is rising.
Boarding desks ask for finished Spanish Water Dog dates, not intentions, so a Spanish Water Dog with only the first DA2PP / DHPP dose is still incomplete for most facilities.
Hip dysplasia shows up often enough in Spanish Water Dogs that vaccine day is also screening day — keep both on the same visit when possible.
Store the rabies label with the Spanish Water Dog profile immediately; lost paperwork is the most common reason Spanish Water Dog travel and kennel check-ins stall.

bodySections.heading: If a dose is missed or delayed
paragraphs: Owners postpone Spanish Water Dog shots when the puppy seems “a little off,” travel intervenes, or hip dysplasia worries dominate the week — ask the clinic whether a same-week Spanish Water Dog make-up is still appropriate instead of sliding to the annual exam.
Long gaps can leave Spanish Water Dog antibody levels uncertain, so expect either an added booster or a titer conversation rather than a shrug.
Do not trade the missed Spanish Water Dog dose for extra socialization; finish immunity first for this medium dog.
Reset the Spanish Water Dog reminder stack the evening of the make-up appointment — including the eventual adult booster after the 16-week finish.

faqs.question: When does the Spanish Water Dog core vaccine series usually finish?
faqs.answer: This breed record completes core vaccines around 16 weeks of age, with rabies timed per local law. Your clinic may adjust intervals for the individual puppy.

faqs.question: What should I do if my Spanish Water Dog misses a booster?
faqs.answer: Contact your veterinarian for a catch-up plan instead of restarting or skipping ahead. Keep prior dates handy and limit high-risk exposure until the series is current again.

faqs.question: Where can I read Spanish Water Dog health context beyond vaccines?
faqs.answer: See the Spanish Water Dog adult health guide for breed predispositions such as hip dysplasia, then bring those notes to wellness and vaccine visits.
